items.title: Finalize the Tier-C threat model + key-management decision doc
items.context: docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-threat-model.md: trust anchor (pinned manifest, verify-against-pinned-not-self), independence definition + honest ceiling (cross-vendor, same-operator), the fail-closed rule table (which become the M1/M2 RED tests), and key gen/pin/rotate/revoke.

happy.desc: Doc contains a pinned-key trust anchor section: verdicts are verified against the PINNED manifest key for the claimed hostId, never the self-reported key in the bundle — reviewer confirms this is stated unambiguously
Independence definition section states cross-vendor (Claude vs Codex, distinct model families and keys) but same-operator ceiling, with allowed vs forbidden paper wording spelled out explicitly

Fail-closed rule table covers all 6 attack vectors: forged verdict, same-key masquerade, stale materialHash, replay, omission, key compromise — each row names detection mechanism and fail-closed response
Key lifecycle section covers generation, pinning, rotation, and revocation procedures as separate subsections with concrete steps
Doc has its own Section 6 acceptance checklist and a reader can derive every fail-closed rule and the independence boundary without external context
Doc references the code-verified current state: CLI-only chain (no Authority server), Ed25519 sign/verify, quorum evaluator in receipt-bundle.ts, decision-doc-quorum.ts, verdicts.ts

edge.desc: Independence ceiling section explicitly distinguishes what the paper MAY claim (cross-vendor independence) vs what it MUST NOT claim (mutually-distrusting multi-party) — the boundary is unambiguous with concrete forbidden phrases listed
Fail-closed table entries are derivable as M1/M2 RED tests: each row names a concrete attack scenario that can be implemented as a test without requiring further threat-model interpretation
Key rotation procedure addresses the transition window where both old and new keys must be valid, and revocation addresses delayed discovery of compromise (not just immediate revocation)
Trust anchor section addresses the bootstrap problem: how the initial pinned manifest is established and by whom, and what happens if the manifest itself is corrupted

adversarial.desc: Doc does NOT contain over-claimed independence wording: phrases like mutually-distrusting parties, fully independent hosts, zero-trust multi-party, or trustless multi-party are absent — grep for these exact phrases must return zero matches

Doc does NOT assume a central Authority server exists for signing or reconciliation — the server is deprecated and the chain is CLI-only; any reference to Authority must be historical or explicitly marked deprecated
Fail-closed table does NOT have a catch-all pass-through, allow-by-default, or best-effort entry — every unrecognized or unhandled case must fail closed
Key compromise row does NOT assume compromise is detectable in real-time — must address the delayed-discovery case where a key was compromised but the operator does not yet know

Doc does NOT conflate key independence (distinct Ed25519 keys) with model independence (distinct vendor/model families) — both are separately required for the cross-vendor claim and named as distinct conditions

verificationEvidence.note: Adversarial grep run on both story-owned docs. 4 of 5 forbidden phrases (fully independent hosts / zero-trust multi-party / trustless multi-party / mutually-distrusting vendor) return ZERO matches. 'mutually-distrusting parties' returns EXACTLY ONE match: threat-model.md line 36, WITHIN the §3 forbidden-phrases list (forbidden = "mutually-distrusting parties" / "no operator trust required") — a meta-use that NAMES the phrase as prohibited for M5 paper wording, NOT an assertion about the system. The prior real over-claim in execution-plan.md ('mutually-distrusting vendor hosts', F-001) was removed in 367b05322, so no assertive occurrence remains. Intent satisfied: the literal grep is non-zero only for the intended forbidden-list definition; the doc set carries no over-claimed independence assertion.

items.title: Finalize the Tier-C cross-host quorum execution plan
items.context: docs/requirements/decisions/tier-c-crosshost-quorum-execution-plan.md: 6-milestone M0-M5 plan, with the cheap proof-of-mechanism block (M0-M3) split from the expensive powered run (M4).

happy.desc: Doc contains a code-verified current-state section naming: CLI-only (no server), existing crypto primitives (Ed25519 sign/verify, quorum evaluator), and the three real gaps (signature-provenance, crypto-independence, cross-host collection)
Doc defines the six-milestone M0-M5 sequence with per-milestone: objective, scope, real files, acceptance criteria, repro-first note, estimated size, and risk
The cheap proof-of-mechanism block (M0-M3) is explicitly split from the expensive powered run (M4) as a separate go/no-go decision gate — the document names this gate and the criteria for proceeding
Each material-code milestone (M1 onward) names concrete real files that will be created or modified — not just abstract descriptions
Doc includes a Lattice-story sequence section showing which Lattice stories map to which milestones

edge.desc: Milestones are ordered with explicit dependencies: M1 depends on M0 threat model, M2 depends on M1, etc. — a reviewer can trace the dependency chain without ambiguity
M4 (powered run) section explicitly states it is deferred and names the preconditions that must be met before it starts, including a cost/benefit justification for the deferral
M5 (if present) has concrete acceptance criteria distinct from M4 — it is not a vague cleanup milestone
Each milestone size estimate is realistic for the scope described (days each for M0-M3, not weeks); if a milestone is larger, a risk note explains why

adversarial.desc: Doc does NOT conflate M0-M3 (cheap mechanism) with M4 (expensive powered run) in a single approval gate — the go/no-go between M3 and M4 must be an explicit separate decision, not implicit
Doc does NOT list milestones without acceptance criteria — every milestone has a concrete, verifiable acceptance condition (not just a task description)
Doc does NOT reference the deprecated Authority server as a live dependency — any mention is historical context only, clearly marked
Doc does NOT claim milestones can be parallelized when they have sequential dependencies — the dependency chain must be honest about what is serial
Real-files lists in material-code milestones do NOT include only .lattice metadata or test fixtures — they name actual source files in packages/ or similar production paths
